text:
ryan: Heads up — saw 3 spot GPU node preemptions in us-west-2 this morning, a few inference pods got evicted and then scheduled onto dedicated-gpu pool which spiked latency. Anyone messing with taints/tolerations or affinity we should know about?

maya: Ugh. Which taint do we use on spot nodes now? I thought it was `node.kubernetes.io/spot=true:NoSchedule`.

sam: Correct — we apply `node.kubernetes.io/spot=true:NoSchedule` on spot pools. Pods that can run on spot need the toleration. If they don't, they'll fall back to dedicated pools if nodeSelector/affinity allows it.

clara: The fallback behaviour is intentional for capacity smoothing, but we hit a problem: our inference deployment has `podAntiAffinity` to spread across racks, so when they moved to dedicated they ended up concentrated and caused GPU OOMs.

ryan: Thought so. We saw a bunch of OOMKilled on the pods after the move. Can we prefer spot but not hard-require it? Want to avoid surprise migrations to dedicated that overload it.

sam: You can do preferredDuringScheduling nodeAffinity to prefer spot nodes but still allow scheduling elsewhere. Example: 
```
nodeAffinity:
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 80
    preference:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: node.kubernetes.io/spot
        operator: In
        values:
        - "true"
```
That plus explicit toleration if you want to schedule on spot. But be careful: toleration alone means pod can be placed on spot when available, and will stay if preempted? Preemptions remove the node, pods die and reschedule.

maya: Another knob is `topologySpreadConstraints` to avoid packing fallback pods onto the same dedicated node. Also check PDB — if PDB is too strict, the scheduler might prefer a busy node instead of evicting.

clara: We also saw Cluster Autoscaler scale-down churn: when spot nodes go away, CA tried to create new spot but we have quota limits so it pushed into dedicated. CA doesn't honor taints automatically — it will create nodes based on pod requests.

k8s-alert-bot: [ALERT] Node ip-10-0-7-22.us-west-2 spotted: preemption event at 2026-03-18T08:12:45Z

ryan: Quick proposal: change inference Deployment to prefer spot + toleration, add soft anti-affinity and topologySpread, and set a lower `maxUnavailable` in the PDB to allow controlled evictions. Also add an autoscaler policy to prefer creating spot nodes first and only fall back to dedicated if spot quota exhausted. Thoughts?

sam: Sounds reasonable. We should also add a pod annotation so our rollout tool can detect when pods are being scheduled on dedicated during scale events: `redwood/scheduled-pool: dedicated|spot` (set via mutating webhook). That'll help alerting.

maya: I can draft the deployment patch. Minimal changes: tolerations + preferred nodeAffinity + topologySpreadConstraints. Will test in staging.

clara: Add these checks to the preflight evals — fail deploy if expected spot capacity < threshold for that release. Prevents surprises.

ops_lead: Also check cost impact: if many inference pods fall back to dedicated GPUs we'll blow monthly committed usage. We need a metric that counts dedicated-GPU-hours caused by fallback so biz can see cost.

ryan: Agreed. For now I'll make a staging change. Example toleration snippet we plan to use: 
```
tolerations:
- key: "node.kubernetes.io/spot"
  operator: "Equal"
  value: "true"
  effect: "NoSchedule"
```
Affinity snippet to prefer spot: 
```
nodeAffinity:
  preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
  - weight: 60
    preference:
      matchExpressions:
      - key: "node.kubernetes.io/spot"
        operator: In
        values:
        - "true"
```
Topology constraint example: 
```
topologySpreadConstraints:
- maxSkew: 1
  topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
  labelSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
```

sam: Nice. One gotcha: if you add toleration but don't set `priorityClass` properly, CA might evict spot pods before other low-priority pods. Consider using a medium priority for inference to reduce preemption churn but not block reclaiming for higher-priority system pods.

maya: I'll run it in staging tomorrow and post results. If staging looks good we'll roll canary to prod with the webhook annotation and alerting on dedicated fallbacks.

ryan: Thanks — tagging @ops_lead to keep an eye on cost dashboards. :thumbsup:

ops_lead: Got it. Keep me posted and please add the dedicated-fallback metric.

clara: Also adding a quick kubectl debug command for whoever investigates next: `kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=app=inference` to see node assignment and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` to check tolerations/affinity.

ryan: Perfect. Closing this thread after the staging run.
